pages.class_justification: One fixed construction (Paillier over $\ZZ_{n^2}^*$) and one fixed reduction: given a DCR challenge $c^*$, the reduction sets the challenge ciphertext to $g^{m_b} \cdot c^*$ and runs any CPA adversary once as an oracle. This is the RTV04 fully-black-box shape.
pages.statement: [[decisional-composite-residuosity|DCR]] implies [[homomorphic-encryption#partially-homomorphic-encryption-phe|additively homomorphic encryption]], the additive fragment of [[homomorphic-encryption|HE]]: the Paillier cryptosystem encrypts $m \in \ZZ_n$ as $c = g^m r^n \bmod n^2$ for $r \getsr \ZZ_n^*$, so $\Enc(\pk, m_1) \cdot \Enc(\pk, m_2) \bmod n^2$ decrypts to $m_1 + m_2 \bmod n$, and it is semantically secure iff DCR is hard — [[Pai99 - Public-key cryptosystems based on composite degree residuosity classes|Pai99]].
pages.sketch: An encryption of $0$ is a uniform $n$-th residue in $\ZZ_{n^2}^*$, which DCR makes indistinguishable from a uniform element of $\ZZ_{n^2}^*$; an encryption of $m$ is $g^m$ times an encryption of $0$, so replacing the residue by a uniform element makes the ciphertext independent of $m$.
pages.security_loss: tight: one call to the CPA adversary

- Threshold decryption for Paillier, the citation for the migrated 'DCR ⇒ threshold encryption' claim — [[FPS00 - Sharing Decryption in the Context of Voting or Lotteries|FPS00]]

sources.note: cryptobib: PKC:DamJur01; source of the fixed choice g = 1+n used in the pseudocode

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction (Paillier) and one fixed reduction: given a DCR challenge $c^*$, the reduction sets the challenge ciphertext to $g^{m_b} \cdot c^*$ and runs any CPA adversary once as an oracle. This is the RTV04 fully-black-box shape.
pages.statement: [[decisional-composite-residuosity|DCR]] implies CPA-secure [[public-key-encryption|PKE]]: the Paillier cryptosystem has public key $(n, g)$ with $n = pq$ an RSA modulus and $g \in \ZZ_{n^2}^*$ of order a nonzero multiple of $n$ ($g = 1+n$ suffices), and encrypts $m \in \ZZ_n$ as $c = g^m r^n \bmod n^2$ for $r \getsr \ZZ_n^*$; the scheme is semantically secure iff DCR is hard — [[Pai99 - Public-key cryptosystems based on composite degree residuosity classes|Pai99]].
pages.sketch: The reduction sets the challenge ciphertext to $g^{m_b} \cdot c^*$ for DCR challenge $c^*$: if $c^*$ is an $n$-th residue this is a correctly distributed encryption of $m_b$, and if $c^*$ is uniform in $\ZZ_{n^2}^*$ the ciphertext is uniform and independent of $b$.

pages.class_justification: The construction is the identity on the group generator; the reduction runs any CDH adversary once as an oracle on $(g^x, g^y)$ and compares its output with the challenge element. One fixed reduction using the adversary only as an oracle: RTV04 fully-black-box.
pages.statement: If [[decisional-diffie-hellman|DDH]] is hard for a group generator $\GrGen$, then [[computational-diffie-hellman|CDH]] is hard for $\GrGen$: a DDH distinguisher runs any CDH adversary on $(g^x, g^y)$ and guesses the real world iff the answer equals the challenge element $Z$ — folklore.
pages.sketch: On DDH challenge $(g^x, g^y, Z)$, run the CDH adversary on $(g^x, g^y)$ and guess the real world iff it returns $Z$. A real tuple is recognised with the adversary's success probability $\varepsilon$; for a random tuple $Z$ is uniform and independent of the adversary's output, so it matches with probability $1/p$. The DDH advantage is therefore at least $\varepsilon - 1/p$.

sources.ref_file_title: Ped91 - Non-Interactive and Information-Theoretic Secure Verifiable Secret Sharing
sources.note: cryptobib: C:Pedersen91; proceedings published 1992. The commitment scheme is Section 3 of the VSS paper.

pages.class_justification: Fixed construction; the reduction is fixed and uses the adversary only as an oracle: on DDH challenge $(X, Y, Z)$ it sets $h = X$, runs the binding adversary to obtain two openings $(m, r) \ne (m', r')$ of one commitment, computes $x = \log_g h = (m - m')(r' - r)^{-1} \bmod p$, and guesses the real world iff $Z = Y^x$. Hiding is perfect, unconditionally.
pages.statement: The Pedersen commitment over $(\GG, g, p) \gets \GrGen(1^\secpar)$ with $h \getsr \GG \setminus \{1\}$ commits to $m \in \ZZ_p$ as $c = g^m h^r$ for $r \getsr \ZZ_p$. It is perfectly hiding, and computationally binding under [[discrete-logarithm|DLOG]] — implied by [[decisional-diffie-hellman|DDH]] via [[ddh-to-cdh|DDH ⇒ CDH]] and [[cdh-to-dlog|CDH ⇒ DLOG]] — since two openings $(m, r) \ne (m', r')$ of one $c$ give $\log_g h = (m - m')(r' - r)^{-1} \bmod p$ — [[Ped91 - Non-Interactive and Information-Theoretic Secure Verifiable Secret Sharing|Ped91]].
pages.sketch: Hiding: $h$ generates $\GG$, so $h^r$ is uniform over $r \getsr \ZZ_p$ and $c$ is uniform, independent of $m$. Binding: two openings of one $c$ yield $\log_g h$, contradicting DLOG for $h$ sampled with unknown discrete logarithm.
pages.security_loss: tight: one call to the binding adversary yields $\log_g h$
flags: HYPOTHESIS STRONGER THAN NEEDED (matches suspected-errors entry for commitment-scheme.md:68): Pedersen binding requires only DLOG; DDH is sufficient but not the right hypothesis. No dlog-to-com page exists in content/Reductions/ — recommend creating dlog-to-com (Ped91) and retiring or demoting this DDH edge.
The statement above is written to be true for the recorded DDH hypothesis (DDH hard ⇒ DLOG hard ⇒ binding); if the edge is re-pointed to DLOG the parenthetical clause should be dropped.

sources.note: DH76 gives the protocol; it predates the DDH assumption, and the DDH-based security statement is a later, definitionally immediate formalization.

pages.class_justification: The construction uses only the group generator and group operations. Against a passive eavesdropper the pair (transcript, key) is a DDH tuple, so the fixed reduction forwards the DDH challenge $(X, Y, Z)$ as transcript $(X, Y)$ with candidate key $Z$ and runs the eavesdropper once as an oracle.
pages.statement: The Diffie–Hellman protocol over $(\GG, g, p) \gets \GrGen(1^\secpar)$: $A$ sends $X = g^a$ and $B$ sends $Y = g^b$ for $a, b \getsr [p]$; both output $k = g^{ab}$. If [[decisional-diffie-hellman|DDH]] is hard for $\GrGen$, then $k$ is computationally indistinguishable from uniform in $\GG$ given the transcript $(X, Y)$ — the DDH definition restated — so the protocol is a [[key-exchange|KE]] secure against passive adversaries — [[DH76 - New Directions in Cryptography|DH76]].
pages.sketch: A distinguisher between $(g^a, g^b, g^{ab})$ and $(g^a, g^b, u)$ for $u \getsr \GG$ is verbatim a DDH distinguisher.

sources.authors: Eduarda S. V. Freire, Dennis Hofheinz, Eike Kiltz, Kenneth G. Paterson
sources.note: cryptobib: PKC:FHKP13; full version eprint 2012/732. Abstract confirmed via WebSearch. Formalizes NIKE and its security models; cited as the reference for the primitive's stronger models, not as an improvement of the DDH reduction itself.

pages.class_justification: Fixed construction from the group generator; the fixed reduction sets $(\pk_i, \pk_j, k_{ij}) := (X, Y, Z)$ from the DDH challenge and runs the adversary once as an oracle.
pages.statement: Diffie–Hellman ([[DH76 - New Directions in Cryptography|DH76]]) is a [[key-exchange#non-interactive-key-exchange-nike|NIKE]]: over $(\GG, g, p) \gets \GrGen(1^\secpar)$, party $i$ samples $x_i \getsr [p]$ and publishes $\pk_i = g^{x_i}$; parties $i$ and $j$ each compute $k_{ij} = \pk_j^{x_i} = \pk_i^{x_j} = g^{x_i x_j}$. For honestly generated keys, indistinguishability of $k_{ij}$ from uniform given $(\pk_i, \pk_j)$ is the [[decisional-diffie-hellman|DDH]] game verbatim — folklore.
pages.sketch: $(\pk_i, \pk_j, k_{ij})$ is a DDH tuple, so a distinguisher for $k_{ij}$ is a DDH distinguisher.
pages.security_loss: tight for one honest pair: the DDH instance is forwarded unchanged
pages.improvements_text: - Formal NIKE security models with adversarially registered keys and their relations, constructions from factoring in the ROM and from a DBDH variant on asymmetric pairings in the standard model, and a generic NIKE ⇒ CCA-secure PKE transformation — [[FHKP13 - Non-Interactive Key Exchange|FHKP13]]
flags: The folklore claim holds in the passive / honest-key-registration setting; in FHKP13's stronger models with dishonest key registration, plain group DH is not proven secure under DDH alone — the statement is scoped accordingly.

sources.ref_file_title: TY98 - On the Security of ElGamal Based Encryption
sources.note: cryptobib: PKC:TsiYun98. WebSearch-confirmed: proves DDH ⇒ semantic security of unmodified ElGamal (messages in the subgroup), the converse, and an exact analysis of the reduction.

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction from the group generator, and one fixed reduction: on DDH challenge $(X, Y, Z)$ set $\pk = X$ and answer the challenge query with $(Y, m_b \cdot Z)$, running the IND-CPA adversary as an oracle. For $Z = g^{xy}$ this is a perfectly distributed encryption of $m_b$; for uniform $Z$ the ciphertext is independent of $b$.
pages.statement: [[decisional-diffie-hellman|DDH]] implies CPA-secure [[public-key-encryption|PKE]]: the ElGamal scheme over $(\GG, g, p) \gets \GrGen(1^\secpar)$ has $\sk = x \getsr [p]$ and $\pk = y = g^x$, encrypts $m \in \GG$ as $(g^r, m \cdot y^r)$ for $r \getsr [p]$, and decrypts $(c_1, c_2)$ as $c_2 \cdot c_1^{-x}$. The scheme is from [[ElGamal85 - A Public Key Cryptosystem and a Signature Scheme Based on Discrete Logarithms|ElGamal85]]; it is semantically secure iff DDH is hard for $\GrGen$ — [[TY98 - On the Security of ElGamal Based Encryption|TY98]].
pages.sketch: On DDH challenge $(X, Y, Z)$ the reduction sets $\pk = X$ and answers the challenge query with $(Y, m_b \cdot Z)$: for $Z = g^{xy}$ this is a correctly distributed encryption of $m_b$, and for uniform $Z$ the ciphertext is uniform and independent of $b$.
pages.improvements_text: - Semantic security of ElGamal proven equivalent to DDH — [[TY98 - On the Security of ElGamal Based Encryption|TY98]]

sources.ref_file_title: NR97 - Number-Theoretic Constructions of Efficient Pseudo-Random Functions
sources.note: cryptobib: FOCS:NaoRei97; journal version J. ACM 51(2), 2004.

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction from the group generator; the security proof is a hybrid over the $n$ input positions in which each step converts a PRF distinguisher, used only as an oracle, into a DDH distinguisher; the polynomially many DDH instances needed per step are generated tightly from one instance via DDH random self-reducibility.
pages.statement: [[decisional-diffie-hellman|DDH]] implies [[pseudorandom-function|PRF]]s: the Naor–Reingold function over $(\GG, g, p) \gets \GrGen(1^\secpar)$ with key $(a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_n) \getsr [p]^{n+1}$ maps $x \in \bits^n$ to $g^{a_0 \prod_{i : x_i = 1} a_i} \in \GG$, and is pseudorandom if DDH is hard for $\GrGen$ — [[NR97 - Number-Theoretic Constructions of Efficient Pseudo-Random Functions|NR97]].
pages.sketch: A hybrid over the $n$ input bits replaces, one level at a time, the contribution of the first $i$ bits by an independent random function of the queried $i$-bit prefixes; a distinguisher between adjacent hybrids yields a DDH distinguisher, the polynomially many DDH samples needed at each level being derived from a single instance by random self-reducibility.
pages.security_loss: factor $n$ over the DDH advantage: one hybrid per input bit, the per-level multi-sample DDH being exact by random self-reducibility
